Building an app with AI? Learn these 4 parts first Want to build an app with AI? Learn the four parts first: the front end, the back end, the database, and where AI fits in a modern app. When you ask ChatGPT or Claude to build you an app (vibe coding, no code), these four parts are what you're actually describing. Explained for complete beginners. We follow one customer message through an online coffee store app, start to finish: 1. Front end: everything the customer sees and taps. The screens, the buttons, the text box. It doesn't know prices or stock. It shows things and passes messages along. 2. Back end: runs on a server the customer never sees. This is where the business rules live: login, stock, prices, payments. The front end asks, the back end decides. 3. Database: where everything is saved, like a giant spreadsheet that never closes. Products, prices, customers, orders. Only the back end opens it, and it checks who's asking. 4. AI in the middle: the back end calls the AI model only for jobs that need understanding. Job one, turn a plain sentence ("a gift for my dad, he drinks it black, under $40") into a search. Job two, write the answer using only the real products the database sent back. The rule for building reliable AI apps: AI handles the words, the back end handles the facts and the money. Never let the AI make up prices or stock. Whole app in four lines: the front end shows, the back end decides, the database remembers, the AI understands and writes. If you want to go from understanding the four parts to building your own apps with AI, I teach it step by step, from complete beginner to real systems. AI can already cut, caption and format a clip for you. Free GitHub skills teach Claude the editing part in minutes. So why isn't everyone going viral off podcast clips? Because editing was never the hard part. Choosing the moment is. AI does not know which 47 seconds out of a two hour conversation deserve to become the clip. No context. No content intelligence. Here is how you build that layer. Scrape the latest 100 clips from the biggest podcast short form accounts. Steven Bartlett, Chris Williamson, Alex Hormozi, anyone running serious long form volume. Capture views, post date, duration, transcript, text overlay and format. Then scrape their original long form episodes and pull the complete transcripts with timestamps. The timestamps are non negotiable. They are what lets Claude match every clip back to the exact episode and the exact moment it came from. Now you reverse engineer the decision. Why those 47 seconds. Where the clip starts. What context got removed. Whether the payoff moved forward. What spoken hook, text overlay and format they used. And how it performed against that account's normal clips. Run enough of these and the patterns surface. Turn the patterns into a Claude skill that understands how the best podcast teams select and package their clips. Then hand it any new timestamped transcript. It returns the strongest moments, exact timestamps, hook options, text overlays, formats and editing instructions. The editing skill does the easy part. None of this needs new software. The tools exist. The clipping skills exist. The data is public. Nobody is assembling it into an intelligence layer. Impossible to fail does not mean every clip goes viral. It means every clip starts with real evidence, and every result makes the next selection smarter. Build the selection layer first. The edit is the easy bit.
